Confirmed: the reconcile loop only *pauses feeds* — it never deletes or deactivates the `connector_definitions` row.

## Answer

They aren't "under" Chrome because in the database they genuinely **are** separate connectors — four independent `connector_definitions` rows, not tools belonging to `chrome`:

| key | name | version | created | capability |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `browser.evaluate` | Browser Evaluate | 0.1.0 | 2026-05-18 | `browser.debugger` |
| `browser.fill_form` | Browser Fill Form | 0.1.0 | 2026-05-18 | `browser.debugger` |
| `browser.page_text` | Browser Page Text | 0.1.0 | 2026-05-18 | `browser.debugger` |
| `chrome.tabs` | Chrome Tabs | 0.1.0 | 2026-05-18 | `browser.tabs` |
| `chrome` | **Chrome** | **0.2.1** | 2026-05-18 | `browser.debugger` |

These are **stale leftovers from the pre-consolidation design.** Originally each browser capability shipped as its own connector. That got folded into the single `chrome` connector — its description says so explicitly (`packages/owletto/apps/chrome/connector-manifests/chrome.json:5`):

> "a fixed set of typed browser actions (navigate, click, type, wait, screenshot, accessibility snapshot, evaluate) that connectors compose **without shipping per-connector code into the extension**"

`evaluate`, `navigate`, `click_ref`, `type_ref`, `screenshot` etc. are now entries in `chrome`'s `actions_schema`, and tabs are the `open_tabs` feed. The only manifests still on disk are `chrome.json`, `chrome_bookmarks.json`, `chrome_downloads.json`, `chrome_history.json` — there is **no** manifest for `browser.evaluate`, `browser.fill_form`, `browser.page_text`, or `chrome.tabs` anymore.

The reason they persist in the UI is that **definition sync has no prune path**. `packages/server/src/worker-api/device-reconcile.ts` upserts definitions the device advertises and, when a capability disappears, only *pauses the auto-wired feeds* (`pauseStaleDeviceFeeds`, line 367) — it never deletes or deactivates the `connector_definitions` row. The rows have sat untouched since 2026-05-18 (`chrome` was updated today, 07-27). The connectors list page (`packages/owletto/src/app/$owner/connectors/index.tsx:153`) then renders one row per definition key, so all four show up as peers of Chrome. Each also has 1 orphaned connection, which is exactly the failure mode called out in `packages/server/src/runs/queue-service.ts:328` and the regression test `sync-run-orphan-feed.test.ts:37` ("a connector with no compiled code and no bundled source file — **the prod `chrome.tabs` state**").

They show "Needs setup" because `deriveConnectorFacets` (line 412) flags any connector with a `required_capability` and no connection group — and no device will ever advertise these keys again, so they can never leave that state.

**This is a data-cleanup issue, not a UI grouping issue.** Nesting them under Chrome would be the wrong fix; they should be removed.

Confidence: **high (90)** that these are stale orphaned rows superseded by `chrome` v0.2.1. Basis: read the live `connector_definitions` table, diffed the key list against the manifests actually on disk, read `chrome.json`'s `actions_schema`, and traced `device-reconcile.ts` to confirm it has no definition-prune path. The repo's own test comments independently name `chrome.tabs` as a known-orphaned prod connector. Not verified: whether those 4 connections carry data anyone still reads, and whether anything references these keys outside this org (I only queried your bound org).

4. Widen the query across all orgs to see how many tenants have these ghost rows, since these were auto-wired per personal org.

**Symptom:** connectors list showed `Browser Evaluate` / `Browser Fill Form` / `Browser Page Text` / `Chrome Tabs` as separate peers of `Chrome`, all "Needs setup", 0 connections.

**Cause:** these were pre-consolidation per-capability connectors, folded into `chrome` v0.2.x (their capabilities are now `chrome`'s `actions_schema` entries — evaluate/click_ref/type_ref — and the `open_tabs` feed). No manifest exists for them on disk anymore. But `packages/server/src/worker-api/device-reconcile.ts` only ever iterates keys the fleet CURRENTLY advertises: a key that vanishes entirely is never visited, so its `connector_definitions` row stays `status='active'` forever. `pauseStaleDeviceFeeds` only pauses feeds; there was no definition-prune path.

**Prod cleanup (2026-07-27):** archived the 4 rows in org `8dc12bdd-…` (`status='archived'`). Their connections were ALREADY soft-deleted back on 2026-05-28. `chrome.tabs` has **357 events** — never hard-delete (`events` append-only). Only 1 org affected; the debris never spread.

**Key schema facts (verified on prod):**
- `connector_definitions.status` CHECK = `active|archived|draft`.
- `idx_connector_defs_org_key` is UNIQUE **partial on `status='active'`** → archiving is fully reversible; a re-advertised key just inserts a fresh active row.
- The connectors list query filters `WHERE d.status = 'active'` (`catalog/connector-definitions.ts`), so archived rows vanish from the UI.

**Traps hit while writing the fix (all cost a test round-trip):**
1. Guarding on "no live connection" NEVER fires — reconcile itself auto-creates the connection. Must scope to rows WE auto-wired (`created_by` = polling user AND `auth_profile_id IS NULL`), the same signature `pauseStaleDeviceFeeds` uses.
2. Guarding on `byKey.size > 0` silently disables the prune: `getBundledDeviceConnectors()` returns `[]` server-side — every `chrome.*`/`apple.*` connector arrives as a DEVICE MANIFEST, not a bundled catalog entry. Gate on a "did the read throw" flag instead.
3. `connections.created_by` is NULLABLE, so `NOT (created_by = $1 AND …)` is NULL for a NULL creator → SQL reads that as "no blocking row" and the archive fires on a connection of unknown provenance. Needs `COALESCE(created_by,'')` to fail CLOSED. The soft-delete UPDATE deliberately uses the bare form (opposite direction — never delete what we can't attribute). Do not unify them.

**Multi-device safety:** `getDeviceManifestSourcesForUser` reads `connector_manifests` from ALL of a user's devices seen in 7 days, and poll only overwrites that column when the body actually has the `connector_manifests` key (`Object.hasOwn`). So a Chrome poll cannot archive the Mac's connectors, and an older client that omits the field keeps its stored manifests.

Complements `runs/queue-service.ts` orphan-feed defense (which soft-deletes the feed reactively after a failed run; this prevents the run existing at all).
